title: Dev update for my arcade flight combat game (it was Broken Meridian, now SALTLINE): rain, a new HUD, motion blur, updated briefing scene
author: KashinHS
selftext:
A few weeks ago I posted the teaser for Broken Meridian [here](https://www.reddit.com/r/aigamedev/comments/1x5r4h5/broken_meridian_ps2era_arcade_flight_combat_built/). I found out that "Broken Meridian" was already taken by another game, so I renamed it to "Saltline" on October 23rd. Yes, I know. The one that blew up recently, but that's a different game. Mine is the one they mentioned on their website (Saltline: one island, one war). Ah well, so here we are, what can you do I guess 😅

This is the first dev update. All of it was added since the teaser:

* **Rain:** one mission has a cloud layer with rain under it. Drops gather on the canopy and run back faster the faster you fly, and the glass dries when you climb back into the sun.
* **Motion blur and a colour grade:** one post pass on the flight camera. The blur shows when you're low and fast or turning hard. The video has it off and on in one picture.
* **New HUD:** the old one got cluttered, the new one aims to be a little more streamlined.
* **Briefing:** I wanted to free the 3D map from its boxy prison and give it a little more space to breathe. 
* **Cutscenes:** I wanted to move away from the static presentation (Text on images) towards a more graphic novel style. This is very much a work in progress.

Same video on YouTube: [https://youtu.be/7Zqg2n5YPBo](https://youtu.be/7Zqg2n5YPBo)

Read more on the dev blog: [https://www.saltlinegame.com/blog/development-update-01/](https://www.saltlinegame.com/blog/development-update-01/)

Feedback is welcome, on the game or on the video.

comments.author: Recoil42
comments.body:
>so I renamed it to "Saltline" on October 23rd

I have to ask: Was Saltline a Claude suggestion?

Broken Meridian sounds better to me fwiw.

replies.author: KashinHS
replies.body:
Hi!

No, it wasn't actually. Broken Meridian was though... probably why it was already taken (I think that one was also made with Claude, so there is that). I thought myself quite witty by abstracting the strait between the two countries to a salty line and thus naming it Saltline (along with renaming the Meridian Accord to Saltline Accord).

But yeah, I liked Broken Meridian more as well.

comments.author: TriumphantConch
comments.body:
I’m probably not your market but I think you need to take some time to think about the name?

I definitely don’t picture this when I hear “Saltline” nor do I get any grasp of what the game is about.

Doesn’t mean it wouldn’t work, but I think better name would help.

replies.author: KashinHS
replies.body: I definitely see your point. I keep thinking about this and might very well change the name again as soon as I find a better one.  Thanks for pointing it out though!

replies.author: TriumphantConch
replies.body: But the game does look good! Wish you best of luck!

comments.author: Advanced_Invite9435
comments.body: How do you do the voices?

replies.author: KashinHS
replies.body:
With a companion tool I built. I will probably open source it once i feel it's stable enough.

It's called Story Studio. You can write scenes in there and manage characters along with a description of how they should sound. You can then create a voice seed from that and use it for the dialogue as soon as you are happy with it.

I started with QwenTTS as the voice engine but soon looked for something else because you can't add directions there without it resulting in a different voice. I then tried VoxCPM but that didn't really work either. It kiiiind of kept the voice but not really. I now settled for Fish Audio Drama3 and that one works well. I still struggle with it sometimes but overall it is quite good.

The LLMs run locally and Story Studio calls them via python scripts. It's already built in a way that you can write an adapter for it that translates its output format to a format your game can work with.
